documents.title: Academic Integrity Policy (file name 2011-03; includes AI language)
documents.summary: A general academic integrity policy that adds AI output to its definition of plagiarism and lists AI use that a faculty member prohibits as cheating. It lets faculty set AI rules and tell students at course start, then covers reporting, appeals and sanctions that apply to all integrity cases.
documents.stance_why: The policy sets no AI default: it counts AI output as cheating only "if prohibited by the faculty member" and says "Faculty members are permitted to have specific policies regarding the use of AI programs, including prohibiting their use", so the decision is delegated to instructors.

units.why: The definition says "outputs of Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) programs when presented as one’s own work" without citation are plagiarism, which classifies unacknowledged AI output as misconduct; P36 fits better than P24 because the point is the violation category, not the disclosure procedure.

units.why: Plagiarism examples list copying "code" or a paper "from another person’s work or AI program’s output without proper citation", so cited AI output is possible and uncited AI output is not; this is a citation duty (P24) rather than a misconduct label because it says what students must do.
units.anchor: or an entire paper from another person’s work or AI program’s output without proper citation

units.policy: Copying, paraphrasing or borrowing code or text from an AI program's output without proper citation and/or acknowledgment, as required by faculty, is plagiarism.

units.why: Cheating includes using AI output for "writing, programming, computer programming, or mathematics assignments if prohibited by the faculty member", so the ban depends on the instructor; P36 (misconduct) fits because it names the act as cheating, with a note that the ban is conditional.

units.policy: Using AI output for any form of academic work, including writing, programming and mathematics assignments, is cheating if the faculty member prohibits it.
units.fit_note: The prohibition applies only where the faculty member prohibits AI; the policy itself sets no default ban.

units.why: The note says "Faculty members are permitted to have specific policies regarding the use of AI programs, including prohibiting their use", which hands the decision to instructors (P04).
